comparison: Current fwp tracing versus checked ARC; identical full HTTP client workloads. No earlier-compiler, C/Rust or timing comparison.
status: All six hosts pass real HTTP comparisons and repeated memory measurements. Four full original jobs pass; the two Windows jobs pass in the linked repair runs after fixing the cancellation-probe header order. Final production acceptance remains separate.
sampling: Current fwp tracing and checked ARC clients perform identical sequential pooled HTTP/2 GET /hello calls against an interpreted loopback server. Each response body is consumed/released and its status contributes 200 to the result. Inputs: 1, 16, 256 calls, cleartext and TLS; three separate instrumented processes per case, with raw interpreter and ordinary native output as controls. Native -O2, ordinary compiler optimization, -ffp-contract=off. Managed allocation requests/bytes, effective retains and allocator-charged peak/final storage start after constant initialization and end after entry execution and cached-value cleanup, before whole-runtime shutdown. GC is disabled and physical freeing enabled in both modes. Pooled connections and detached I/O tasks can remain at this sample. Raw network buffers, TLS/allocator/OS metadata, server memory, process RSS and timing are excluded. This compares memory modes at one revision, not before/after speed or C/Rust parity. Source, ordinary and instrumented C/binaries and raw results are retained.
cost_definition: Managed allocation requests and effective retains include iterator/fold work, environment reads, request/options construction, URL parsing, connection selection and received response storage. They do not isolate raw HTTP/2 transport. The final sample precedes full runtime shutdown and includes pooled connection/task storage.

validation.windows_repair_result: Both full HTTP ownership, real-call and steady-memory suites pass; runtime/compiler source unchanged from the measurement revision.

machine_code_review.method: Static file/symbol/section/disassembly inspection using LLVM tools; no downloaded binary executed. scripts/inspect-http-client-binaries.py reproduces the 48-binary inspection. Linux O2 HTTP entry is f330 in retained source and machine code.

linux_amd64.frame_instructions: Six register pushes plus subq $0x268, %rsp, in both modes; excludes incoming return address and callees.
linux_amd64.arc_registers: Pool key held in R14, incoming transport in R13; request pointer spills to the stack. Request owner uses stack slots at SP+0x20/0x28, with its linked cleanup record at SP+0x8/0x10/0x18. These are ordinary allocation decisions, not fallback behavior.

linux_arm64.frame_instructions: 96-byte saved-register area plus sub sp,sp,#0x270, in both modes; excludes callees.
linux_arm64.arc_registers: Pool key held in X21, request in X24 and incoming transport in X19 during startup.

machine_code_review.code_growth: On Linux AMD64, the 532 common generic function-value entries grow by 204649 instruction bytes in total. For example e190 grows from 126 to 1057 bytes: tracing calls fwp_rc_share, while ARC inlines its counted-owner contract checks repeatedly. Other removed/changed code affects the total. This is measured code size, not a claim about execution time or instruction-cache misses.
machine_code_review.limits: Symbols alone do not prove every lifetime. Failure, cancellation, stress and interpreter comparisons are separate tests. Managed counters exclude raw transport/TLS/OS memory and process RSS; no speed or C/Rust parity claim.
